rationale: P characterises whether required collision-avoidance braking occurs in the declared hazardous situation, which directly addresses T. Braking behaviour itself is established as the subject of evaluation by SG-1 and FR-7. Its timeliness is supported by H-1's hazardous event of failing to stop in time, rather than inferred from sensing or processing deadlines. P does not incorporate supporting observation, computation, communication, or control mechanisms.
determining_elements: Required braking behaviour and its presence or absence directly correspond to preventing omitted braking maneuvers under SG-1 and performing collision-avoidance braking under FR-7.
The declared scope reproduces H-1's operational situation: straight-ahead driving at 50 km/h on a less frequented single-lane road in good weather, with a pedestrian crossing 20 m ahead.
The inclusion of 'failure to brake in time' concerns the braking phenomenon's own temporal behaviour, supported by H-1's failure-to-stop-in-time hazardous event.
The scope remains focused on obstacle-avoidance braking rather than incorporating detection, sensor fusion, failure monitoring, warnings, or architectural data flows.
